Single-phase AC path

Current, voltage, and power factor feeding a real watt result

AC pages need power factor context, so the visual connects outlet voltage, current draw, PF, and breaker planning.

Formula kW = Watts / 1000

Quick answer

Use this calculator to convert AC current into real watts with voltage and power factor.

Single-phase AC loads can be resistive or inductive. Resistive loads may be near PF 1.00, while motors, compressors, and HVAC equipment often need a lower power factor.

kW = Watts / 1000

Inputs to check before calculating

  • Use the correct nominal voltage for the circuit.
  • Enter measured current or nameplate running current.
  • Use realistic PF for motors, compressors, and transformer loads.
  • Compare the result with breaker and continuous-load limits.

Example: 10 amps at 240 volts

At 240 volts, 10 amps equals 2.4 kW before AC power-factor adjustments.

Best use cases

  • Fast kW conversion
  • AC and DC support
  • Load planning result
  • single-phase AC load planning with clear unit labels.

Common mistake to avoid

Do not use DC-style amps x volts for every AC load when the equipment has a lower power factor.

How to use the result

Use the watt result for appliance planning, branch-circuit checks, and comparison with the main amps to watts formula.

Accuracy and safety note

Calculator output is a planning estimate. Final breaker sizing, wire gauge, derating, voltage-drop limits, equipment protection, and code compliance should be verified with manufacturer documentation and a qualified electrician or engineer.

Methodology, Review Notes, and Sources

How this calculator works

The calculator applies Watt's law for DC and resistive loads, then adds power factor for AC loads and the 1.732 multiplier for balanced three-phase line-to-line calculations.

  • DC and resistive loads: W = A x V
  • Single-phase AC: W = A x V x PF
  • Three-phase AC: W = 1.732 x A x V x PF

FAQ

Amps to kW FAQ

Fast answers before you use the calculator or compare formulas.

kW How do I convert amps to kilowatts?

First convert amps to watts (Watts = Amps × Volts × PF), then divide by 1,000: kW = Watts ÷ 1,000. Example: 30A at 240V with PF 1.0 = 7,200W = 7.2 kW. The calculator does both steps automatically.

kWh What is the difference between kW and kWh?

kW is a rate of power (how fast energy is used). kWh is an amount of energy (total energy consumed over time). A 2 kW heater running for 3 hours uses 6 kWh. Your electricity bill charges per kWh. kW tells you the instantaneous load; kWh tells you the total consumption.

1kW How many amps is 1 kW at 240V?

1 kW (1,000 watts) at 240V with PF 1.0 draws 1,000 ÷ 240 = 4.17 amps. With a motor load at PF 0.85: 1,000 ÷ (240 × 0.85) = 4.90 amps. The lower the power factor, the more current is needed for the same real power.

PRO Why is kW used more than watts in professional settings?

Professional and industrial equipment commonly operates in the thousands of watts, making kilowatts more practical. Generator ratings (5 kW, 20 kW), motor power (1.5 kW, 7.5 kW), utility metering (kWh), and HVAC sizing all use kW. It is simply watts ÷ 1,000.

$ How do I calculate electricity cost from amps?

Convert amps to kW (kW = Amps × Volts × PF ÷ 1,000). Multiply by hours of use to get kWh. Multiply by your electricity rate ($/kWh). Example: 10A heater on 120V for 8 hours at $0.15/kWh: (10 × 120 ÷ 1,000) × 8 × 0.15 = $1.44 per day.

3P What is the amps to kW formula for three-phase?

kW = (√3 × Amps × Volts × PF) ÷ 1,000. For 20A at 480V three-phase with PF 0.88: kW = (1.732 × 20 × 480 × 0.88) ÷ 1,000 = 14.6 kW. This is the total real power across all three phases.
